title: Boys Town Centennial Commemorative Coin Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on June 23, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Boys Town Centennial Commemorative Coin Act

(Sec. 3) Directs the Secretary of the Treasury to mint and issue up to 50,000 $5 gold coins, 350,000 $1 silver coins, and 300,000 half-dollar clad coins to commemorate the centennial of the founding of Father Flanagan's Boys Town.

(Sec. 4) Requires the design of the coins to be emblematic of the 100 years of Boys Town, one of the largest nonprofit child care agencies in the United States.

(Sec. 5) Permits issuance of such coins only between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2017.

(Sec. 7) Subjects all coin sales to specified surcharges, which shall be paid to Boys Town to carry out its cause of caring for and assisting children and families in underserved communities across America. Prohibits any surcharge if issuance of the coin would exceed the annual commemorative coin program issuance limitation.

(Sec. 8) Directs the Secretary to ensure that: (1) minting and issuing such coins will not result in any net cost to the federal government; and (2) no funds, including surcharges, will be disbursed to Boys Town until the total cost of designing and issuing all authorized coins is recovered by the Treasury.

summary.headline: Authorizes special 2017 commemorative coins marking Boys Town's 100th anniversary, with coin sale surcharges paid to the nonprofit.
summary.what_it_does: The law lets the Treasury Secretary mint up to 50,000 $5 gold coins, 350,000 $1 silver coins, and 300,000 half-dollar coins. The coins must have a design that represents Boys Town's first 100 years. They can be issued only during calendar year 2017. Each sale carries a surcharge that goes to Boys Town for its work with children and families in underserved communities. The Treasury must ensure the program costs the federal government nothing, and Boys Town receives no money until the cost of designing and issuing all the coins is repaid.

who_it_affects.how: They can buy these limited-run gold, silver, and half-dollar coins, but only during 2017.

who_it_affects.group: Boys Town and the children and families it serves
who_it_affects.how: The nonprofit receives surcharge money from coin sales, but only after the Treasury recovers its design and minting costs.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. Treasury and the U.S. Mint
who_it_affects.how: They must design, mint, and issue the coins in a way that results in no net cost to the federal government.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Became law on July 6, 2015; coins may be issued only from January 1 through December 31, 2017.
